chapter_title: Appendix D: Sample Problem No. 1, Bridge Foundation Abutment Support

sections.title: Sample Problem No. 1 – Bridge Abutment Foundation Support
sections.body:
[p. D-1] The following sample problem illustrates the design of foundation support for a bridge abutment using micropiles. This sample problem is intended to illustrate the quantification of typical abutment loads and the design of a micropile foundation for non-seismic load groups. In the example, seismic loads are provided and the example could be repeated using these loads. Practitioners typically follow different procedures around the United States in the design of bridge abutments, and therefore this sample problem is not intended to depict a “standard abutment” or a “standard abutment design procedure.” For simplicity, this example problem considers only a portion of the longitudinal forces and no transverse forces. Abutment designs, which include wind or seismic forces, for example, would have transverse as well as longitudinal forces. This example also does not illustrate construction load cases (e.g., full backfill prior to girder placement) that need to be incorporated into actual designs.

Problem Statement

The structure is a simply supported, single-span bridge, 30 meters long, supported on concrete retaining abutments. The superstructure consists of 5 AASHTO Type IV precast - prestressed concrete girders with a cast-in-place concrete deck.

The bridge abutment length is 10.5 meters. The abutment wall backfill material is medium dense sand with an angle of internal friction of 35 degrees and a unit weight of 17.5 kN/m³. The unit weight of the concrete is 23.6 kN/m³. Figure S1-1 shows the dimensions of the abutment. The pile details are shown on Figure S1-2.

A summary of loading applied to the bridge abutment is shown in Figure S1-3. All load values are per 1-meter length of the abutment. The seismic site coefficient is 0.1 g.

The foundation soil conditions are described in the boring log contained in Figure S1-4. These soils consist of 2.5 meters of loose sandy gravel underlain by moderately compressible soft, brown, fine sandy silt, which is 1.5 meters thick. The silt is underlain by dense to very dense gravel with cobbles and boulders that extends to a maximum depth of 30 meters. Ground water is 4 meters below the top of footing. Type B3 (pressure grouted through the casing during casing withdrawal) micropiles will be used. The bond length will be formed in the dense gravel.

sections.title: Step 1 – Abutment Design Loads
sections.body:
[p. D-6] The magnitude and point of application for the active earth pressure, earth pressure due to live load surcharge, and seismic earth pressure is determined in this section. Calculations for the remaining components of the abutment loading are not included. The magnitude, point of application, and resulting moment on the abutment for the entire load components are summarized in Table S1-1. The moments are taken about the center point of the base of the abutment footing.

Active Earth Pressure - PE

Soil internal friction angle φ = 35 degrees

Unit weight of soil γsoil = 17.5 kN/m³

Coefficient of active soil pressure Ka = tan²[45° - φ/2] = 0.271

Ka γsoil = 4.74 kN/m³

Resultant load PE = 0.5 × 4.74 kN/m³ × (5.25m)² = 65.32 kN/m

Moment about centroid 65.32 kN/m × 5.25m/3 = 114.31 kN-m/m

Earth Pressure Due to Live Load Surcharge - HL

Surcharge pressure Ka × γsoil × 0.6m = 2.84 kPa

Surcharge load 2.84 kN × 5.25m = 14.91 kN/m

Moment about centroid 14.91 kN/m × 5.25m/2 = 39.1 kNm/m

[p. D-7] [Table S1-1]

Seismic Earth Pressure - PEQ

See “Seismic Design of Bridges - Design Example No. 3" Publication No. FHWA-SA-97-008 for a description of the following Mononobe - Okabe lateral seismic earth over pressure and the seismic inertia forces from the abutment self-weight and the soil resting on the abutment footing.

Seismic acceleration coefficient: A = 0.10

Seismic coefficients kh = 1.5 × A = 0.15 and kv = 0 (assumed value)

Reference AASHTO Sec. 6.4.3 (A) Div. 1A.

Slope of soil face: β = 0°

[p. D-8] Backfill slope angle: i = 0°

Friction angle between soil and abutment: δ = ½ φ = 17.5°

Seismic inertia angle θ = tan⁻¹[kh / (1 - kv)] = 8.53°

Seismic earth pressure coefficient

Ψ = [1 + √(sin(φ + δ) × sin(φ - θ - i) / (cos(δ + β + θ) × cos(i - β)))]² = 2.65

KAE = [cos²(φ - θ) / (Ψ × cos(θ) × cos(θ + δ))] = 0.34

Seismic earth pressure KAE γsoil = 5.95 kN/m³

Resultant seismic force PEQ = [0.5 × 5.95 kN/m³ × (5.25m)²] - PE = 16.68 kN/m

Since this force is at angle δ to the horizontal,

PEQ-H = 16.68 kN/m (cos δ) = 15.91 kN/m

To be conservative, neglect the vertical portion of PEQ over the footing heel.

Seismic Inertia Forces

IA = kh (DC + DS) = 0.15 × (97.0 + 108.68) = 30.9 kN/m

IS = kh (VDL) = 0.15 × 178.70 = 26.8 kN/m

Moment about centroid: 16.68 kN/m × 0.6 × 5.25m = 52.54 kNm/m (as printed; Table S1-1 gives the moment of the horizontal component, PEQ-H: 15.91 × 3.15 = 50.12 kN-m)

sections.title: Step 2 – Determine Pile Design Loads per Meter Length
sections.body:
[p. D-9] The Group I loads per AASHTO Table 3.22.1A are calculated from the abutment loads shown in Table 5-4 (as printed; the abutment loads are in Table S1-1).

Fy = sum of vertical loads

Fx = sum of horizontal loads

M = sum of moments about the center of the footing at its base.

Fy = DC + DS + VDL + VLL

Fy = 97.0 + 108.7 + 178.7 + 73.0 = 457.4 kN/m

Fx = HL + PE

Fx = 15.0 + 65.3 = 80.3 kN/m (as printed; Table S1-1 gives HL = 14.91 kN, and 14.91 + 65.32 = 80.23)

M = DC + DS + VDL + VLL + HL + PE

M = 26.2 - 59.8 + 103.7 + 42.3 + 39.3 + 114.3 = 266.0 kN/m (as printed; Table S1-1 gives 39.13 for HL, and its six moments sum to 265.85)

Determine Pile Group Properties Per Meter Length

Centroid of Pile Group (from front pile)

Front piles: 1/1.5 × 0.0 = 0.0

Rear piles: 1/2.25 × 1.85 = 0.822

Sum: 1.111; 0.822

So centroid is (0.822/1.111) = 0.74 m from front pile.

[p. D-10] e = 1.85/2 - 0.74 = 0.185 m

Pile Group I about centroid

I = 1/1.5 (0.74)² + 1/2.25 (1.11)² = 0.9127

Rear Pile Vertical Load = [Fy/1.111 - (M - Fy e) 1.11 / 0.9127]

Front Pile Vertical Load = [Fy/1.111 + (M - Fy e) 0.74 / 0.9127]

Group I Pile Design Loads

Rear Pile Vertical Load = [457.4/1.111 - [266 - 457.4 × 0.185] 1.11 / 0.9127] = 191 kN

Front Pile Vertical Load = [457.4/1.111 + [266 - 457.4 × 0.185] 0.74 / 0.9127] = 559 kN

Front Pile Axial Load = 559 / cos(20°) = 595 kN compression

(Controlling Group 1, non-seismic, axial design load per pile)

A more refined analysis would utilize the vertical stiffness of the batter pile.
sections.applicability: Printed STEP 2 (pp. D-9 to D-10): the Group I sums Fy, Fx and M, the pile group centroid, eccentricity and moment of inertia per meter, and the rear and front pile loads (595 kN axial on the battered front pile).

sections.title: Step 3 – Evaluate Allowable Structural Capacity of Cased Length
sections.body:
[p. D-11] A single pile design is used that can support the maximum compression load that acts on the front row of battered piles.

For the permanent casing reinforcement, a yield strength of 241 MPa is used for design. To maintain strain compatibility between the reinforcing bar and casing in the upper pile length, a yield strength (Fy-steel) of 241 MPa is used for both members. The use of a higher strength casing, such as API N80 (Fy = 552 MPa) would greatly increase the structural capacity of this section of the pile. These calculations do not address the capacity of the casing joint.

If the project incorporated a larger number of piles, savings could be realized by the use of separate designs for the front and rear piles. For example, a smaller casing size and a shorter bond length may be used on the rear piles due to the lower required capacity. The use of separate designs could increase the amount of load testing required at the start of the project, which the potential savings on a larger piling job could support. Consideration must also be given to maintaining simple pile construction. Mixing different reinforcing sizes and pile depths can occasionally lead to errors during pile installation. Also, if the overall stiffness (load versus pile top deflection) of the pile is changed, then the centroid and load per pile must be reevaluated.

Pile Cased Length Allowable Load

Material dimensions and properties

Casing - Use 141 mm outside diameter x 9.5 mm wall thickness.

Reduce outside diameter by 1.6 mm to account for corrosion.

Casing outside diameter ODcasing = 141 mm - 2 x 1.6 mm = 137.8 mm

Pile casing inside diameter IDcasing = 141 mm - 2 x 9.5 mm = 122 mm

Pile casing steel area Acasing = π/4 [OD²casing - ID²casing] = 3,224 mm²

Casing yield strength Fy-casing = 241 MPa

[p. D-12] Radius of gyration rcasing = √(OD² + ID²) / 4 = 46 mm

Reinforcing bar - Use 43 mm grade 520 steel reinforcing bar.

Bar area Abar = 1,452 mm²

Bar steel yield strength Fy-bar = 520 MPa

Grout area Agrout = π/4 ID²casing - Abar = 10,240 mm²

Grout compressive strength f′c-grout = 34.5 MPa

For strain compatibility between casing and rebar, use for steel yield stress:

Fy-steel = the minimum of Fy-bar and Fy casing = 241 MPa

Allowable Tension Load

Pt-allowable = 0.55 Fy-steel (Abar + Acasing) = 620 kN

Allowable Compression Load

Pc-allowable = [0.4 f′c-grout × Agrout + 0.47 Fy-steel (Abar + Acasing)] = 671 kN
sections.applicability: Printed STEP 3 (pp. D-11 to D-12): the 141 mm x 9.5 mm casing with 1.6 mm corrosion loss, the 43 mm Grade 520 bar, Fy-steel = 241 MPa for strain compatibility, and the allowable tension and compression loads of the cased length (Eqs. 5-1 and 5-2).

sections.title: Step 4 – Evaluate Allowable Structural Capacity of Uncased Length
sections.body:
[p. D-12] Pile Uncased Length Allowable Load

Material dimensions and properties

Soil conditions and the method of pile installation can affect the resulting diameter of the pile bond length. For this example, assume a drill-hole diameter of 50 mm greater than the casing outside diameter (OD).

[p. D-13] Using a casing OD = 141mm

Therefore, Grout Db = 141 mm + 50 mm = 191 mm (0.191 m)

Bond length grout area Agrout = π/4 D²b - Abar = 27,200 mm²

Allowable Tension Load

Pt-allowable = 0.55 Fy-bar × Abar = (0.55 × 520 MPa × 1,452 mm²) = 415 kN

Allowable Compression Load

Pc-allowable = (0.4 f′c × Agrout + 0.47 Fy-bar × Abar)

Pc-allowable = (0.4 × 34.5 MPa × 27,200 mm² + 0.47 × 520 MPa × 1,452 mm²) = 730 kN
sections.applicability: Printed STEP 4 (pp. D-12 to D-13): the 191 mm bond length grout diameter and the allowable tension and compression loads of the uncased length (Eqs. 5-7 and 5-8).

sections.title: Step 5 – Evaluate Allowable Geotechnical Capacity
sections.body:
[p. D-13] Allowable Load – Geotechnical Capacity

The micropile bond length will be located in the dense to very dense sandy gravel with cobbles and boulders starting approximately 3.35 m below the bottom of footing elevation. The pile bond length shall be installed using a Type B pressure grouting methodology.

From Table 5-3 select an ultimate unit grout-to-ground bond strength α bond = 265 kPa. This represents an approximate average value for gravels.

The controlling non-seismic micropile loading is 595 kN per pile. Therefore, an allowable geotechnical bond load PG-allowable ≥ 595 kN/pile must be provided to support the structural loading.

Provide: PG-allowable ≥ 595 kN/pile

Compute the bond length, Lb, required to provide PG-allowable as follows:

[p. D-14] Lb = PG-allowable × FS / (αbond × π × Db)

Lb = 595 kN × 2.0 / (265 kPa × π × 0.191 m) = 7.48 m

Select Bond Length = 7.5 m

PG-allowable = 265 kPa / 2.0 × 3.14 × 0.191m × 7.5m = 596 kN
sections.applicability: Printed STEP 5 (pp. D-13 to D-14): the bond strength from Table 5-3 (265 kPa in gravel, Type B grouting), the bond length for FS = 2.0 (Eq. 5-10) and the allowable geotechnical load.

sections.title: Step 6 – Verify Allowable Loads
sections.body:
[p. D-14] The controlling axial design load for the pile is 595 kN (compression). The summary of the pile allowable loads is:

Structural Upper Cased Length = 671 kN (compression)

Structural Lower Uncased Length = 730 kN (compression)

Geotechnical Bond Length = 596 kN (compression)

The allowable loads are all greater than the 595 kN design load, therefore the pile axial design is OK.

The controlling lateral design load is 80.3 kN/m. Check to see if the batter piles carry lateral loads. The front row of piles are battered at 20° from vertical and each pile carries the following ratio of the vertical pile load as a lateral resisting load.

Lateral resisting load = 559 kN × tan(20°) = 204 kN per pile

The lateral design load per pile = 80.3 kN/m × (1.5m) = 120 kN per pile

The lateral resisting load is greater than the lateral design load therefore the pile lateral design is OK.
sections.applicability: Printed STEP 6 (p. D-14): the allowable loads against the 595 kN design load, and the lateral resistance of the battered front piles against the lateral design load.

sections.title: Step 7 – Estimate Micropile Settlement
sections.body:
[p. D-15] Settlements resulting from consolidation of soil layers below the micropile group are not anticipated as these soils are not cohesive in nature. Herein, elastic settlements are calculated.

Casing Length Elastic Stiffness

Front pile batter angle Φbatter = 20°

Max pile length from footing to top of gravel Lupper = 3.35 m / cos(Φbatter) = 3.6 m

Casing insertion into bond length Linsert = 1.0 m

Pile casing length Lcasing = Lupper + Linsert = 4.6 m

Steel modulus of elasticity Esteel = 200,000 MPa

Grout modulus of elasticity Egrout = 31,000 MPa

Area of Grout Agrout = 10,240 mm²

Asteel = Abar + Acasing = 1,452 mm² + 3,224 mm² = 4,676 mm²

Pile compression stiffness value

EAcased length = Agrout × Egrout + Asteel × Esteel = 1,252,000 kN (as printed; 10,240 × 31,000 + 4,676 × 200,000 N gives 1,252,640 kN)

Uncased Length Elastic Stiffness

Pile uncased length (bond length) Lb = 7.5 m

Asteel = Abar = 1,452 mm²

Agrout = 27,200 mm²

Pile compression stiffness value

[p. D-16] EAuncased length = Agrout × Egrout + Asteel × Esteel = 1,133,000 kN (as printed; 27,200 × 31,000 + 1,452 × 200,000 N gives 1,133,600 kN)

Elastic Displacement

Elastic displacement (cased length)

Δtelastic = Pcompression × Lcasing / AEcased length = 595 kN × 4.6 m / 1,252,000 kN = 2.2 mm

Elastic displacement (uncased length)

Δtelastic = Pcompression × Lb / AEuncased length = 595 kN × (1/2 × 7.5 m) / 1,133,000 kN = 2.0 mm
sections.applicability: Printed STEP 7 (pp. D-15 to D-16): the axial stiffness of the cased and uncased lengths and their elastic displacements.

sections.title: Step 8 – Micropile to Footing Connection Design
sections.body:
[p. D-16] Design calculations are completed for the detail shown in Figure S1-5 for connection of the pile top to the abutment footing.

Required Design Loads and Dimensions

Group I service load, compression Pc-service = 595 kN

Abutment concrete compressive strength f’c = 27.6 MPa

Casing outside diameter ODcasing = 141 mm

Pile area Areapile = π/4 OD²casing = 15,615 mm²

[p. D-17] Required Plate Area

Assume a 254 mm square plate Areaplate = Plate²width = 64,516mm²

Check Cone Shear

Sketch (not numbered in the print): 400 mm cover depth; d1 = 286 mm; d2 = 286 + 2 x 400 = 1,086 mm; Pcone allowable; slopes 1:1

Pcone allowable ≥ Pc-service = 595 kN

[p. D-18] Equivalent diameter for 254 mm² plate, = √(4 × 254² / π) = 286mm (as printed; √(4 × 254² / π) = 286.6)

ACP = π/4 [d2² - d1²] = π/4 [1086² - 286²] = 862,053 mm²

Use ACI 349 Appendix B for cone shear

Pcone design strength = 4 φ √(f′c psiCP) x Acp (as printed)

= 4 φ √(f′c psi (6.89476) kPa/psi) x Acp

= 10.5 φ √(f′c) kPa × ACP

Pcone nominal strength = 10.5 φ √(f′c) kPa × ACP (as printed; the line below leaves φ out, and φ enters through FS = LF/φ)

= 10.5 √(27.6 mPa) (1000kPa / mPa) × ACP × 10⁻⁶

= 1,504 kN

Pcome allowable = Pcome noninal strength / FS (as printed)

FS = LF / φ

LF = Combined load factor = γ [BD QD + BL QL + BE QE] / [QD + QL + QE]

Where: γ = 1.3; BD = 1; BL = 1.67; BE = 1.3

and with QD = 0.62; QL = 0.16; QE = 0.22

[p. D-19] QD / (QD + QL + QE) = 0.62

QL / (QD + QL + QE) = 0.16

QE / (QD + QL + QE) = 0.22

LF = 1.3 [1.0 × 0.62 + 1.67 × 0.16 + 1.3 × 0.22] = 1.53

φ = 0.65 for unreinforced shear cone per ACI 349 Appendix B

FS = 1.53 / 0.65 = 2.35

Pcone allowable = 1,504 kN / 2.35 = 640 kN > 594.6 kN .... OK

Note – edge distance limitations and other requirements of ACI 349 Appendix B must be satisfied.

Required Plate Thickness

Actual bearing stress, compression Bearingcompression = Pc-service / Areaplate = 9.22 MPa

Plate bending moment for 10 mm width

Mmax = 10 mm × 1/2 [(Platewidth - ODcasing) / 2]² × Bearingcompression = 0.147 kNm

Note - use of this cantilever moment was determined to be a conservative approximation of the maximum moment in the plate due to a compression pile load by comparison to a [p. D-20] more accurate formula shown in Roark and Young (1975). Plate bending from a tension pile load or with different plate support details must be further analyzed.

Allowable bending stress - Fy = 345 MPa and Fb = 0.55Fy

Note - Allowable stresses should be increased by the appropriate % factor (AASHTO Table 3.22.1A column 14) depending on which load group produces controlling load condition. For this example, the Group I load produces the controlling condition (% = 100%).

Sx-req = Mmax / Fb = 775mm³

Required plate thickness - treq = √(6 Sx-req / 10 mm) = 21.6 mm

Use 254 mm square x 25.4 mm thick top plate.

Required Weld Size:

Tensile strength of E70 electrode, Fuweld = 483 MPa

Minimum tensile strength of connected parts (ASTM A53 Grade B Casing)

Fupart = 414 MPa

Fillet weld strength ΦF = 0.27 Fupart = 111.8 MPa

Top weld size tweld-top = 6.35mm

Stiffener plate size tstiff = 12.7 mm Wstiff = 100 mm Lstiff = 150 mm

Top weld strength Lweld = π ODcasimg - 4 tstiff + 8 Wstiff = 1,190 mm

Top weld strength

Pweld-top = 0.707 tweld-top Φ F Lweld = 598 kN > 595 kN . . . OK

[p. D-21] Stiffener plate side weld dimensions tweld-side = 6.35mm

Lweld = 8 Lstiff = 1,200 mm

Stiffener plate side weld strength

Pweld-side = 0.707 tweld-side ΦFweld Lweld = 603 kN (as printed; 0.707 × 6.35 × 111.8 × 1,200 = 602,305 N, 602 kN)

> 0.707 tweld-top ΦF × 8 Wstiff = 402 kN . . . . OK

Use 6.35 mm fillet weld for welding top and stiffener plates.

Note - this example ignored bending stresses on the welds which is considered appropriate for a compression pile load with the weld details shown. Weld bending stress must be analyzed for other conditions.

sections.title: Step 9 – Check Structural Capacity to Resist Test Loads
sections.body:
[p. D-21] The controlling axial design load for the pile is 595 kN (compression).

Verification Test Load = 2.0 × Design Load

= 2.0 × 595 kN = 1,190 kN

Proof Test Load = 1.6 × Design Load

= 1.6 × 595 kN = 952 kN

[p. D-22] Cased Length: OD* = 141mm; ID = 122 mm (9.5 mm wall); Acasing = 3,925 mm²; Fy-casing = 241 MPa (use for casing and bar); Abar = 1,452 mm²; Fy-bar = 520 MPa; Agrout = 10,240 mm²; f’c-grout = 34.5 MPa

Uncased Length: Agrout = 27,200 mm²; f’c-grout = 34.5 MPa; Abar = 1,452 mm²; Fy-bar = 520 MPa

* Do not reduce by 1.6 mm for corrosion.

Pile Cased Length Allowable Load

Pc-allowable = [0.68 f′c-grout Agrout + Fy-casing / 1.25 (Abar + Acasing)]

Pc-allowable = [0.68 × 34.5MPa × 10,240 mm² + 241MPa / 1.25 (1,452 mm² + 3,925 mm²)] = 1,277 kN

Pile Uncased Length Allowable Load

Pc-allowable = 0.68 f′c-grout Agrout + 0.80 Fy-bar Abar

Pc-allowable = 0.68 × 34.5 MPa × 27,200 mm² + 0.80 × 520 MPa × 1,452 mm² = 1,242 kN

The design pile is OK for the proof test at 952 kN and the verification test at 1,190 kN.
sections.applicability: Printed STEP 9 (pp. D-21 to D-22): verification (2.0 x design load) and proof (1.6 x design load) test loads against the structural capacity of the cased and uncased lengths.
